feature.title: AHA 2026 Delivers Landmark AI Trial Results: Cardiology's Clinical Evidence Moment Has Arrived
feature.summary: The week of November 6–12, 2026 marks a watershed in clinical AI, with the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions in Chicago serving as the stage for multiple late-breaking randomized trial readouts. The PARAMOUNT trial — the world's first randomized study of AI-guided coronary plaque-based care — met its primary endpoint with a 2.00 win ratio over standard stress testing, while Cordio Medical's DETECT-HF study validated voice AI in 563 patients for predicting heart failure 24.6 days in advance. Simultaneously, Kaiser Permanente's AI ECHO INSIGHT trial showed AI-drafted echocardiogram reports cut cardiologist reading time 46% with non-inferior accuracy. Outside cardiology, Virtuoso Surgical's robotic endoscopy system won FDA de novo authorization for bladder tumor resection and Bechtel Medical's Wound VOX became the first combined negative pressure and topical oxygen therapy cleared by the FDA — both entering commercial rollout.

highlights.label: Biggest story
highlights.text: Cleerly's PARAMOUNT RCT — the first AI-guided coronary plaque trial — met its primary endpoint at AHA 2026, with lipid-lowering therapy use jumping from 31% to 75% in the AI arm versus 32% to 47% in usual care.

highlights.label: Key trend
highlights.text: Clinical AI is graduating from pilot to randomized trial evidence, with AHA 2026 producing validated results across chest pain triage, heart failure voice monitoring, and echocardiography workflow — none established purely on bench data.

highlights.label: To watch
highlights.text: Cordio Medical's HearO voice AI is heading for FDA submission after DETECT-HF, and Virtuoso Surgical plans its focused US robot rollout in 2027 — both are pipeline-to-deployment transitions to monitor closely.

articles.title: PARAMOUNT: First Randomized Trial of AI-Enabled Coronary Plaque-Based Care Meets Primary Endpoint at AHA 2026
articles.snippet: Cleerly's PARAMOUNT trial — randomizing 523 patients with stable chest pain across 21 US sites — found AI-quantitative coronary CT analysis (AI-QCT) favored over usual stress testing with a win ratio of 2.00 (95% CI 1.37–2.56, p<0.0001). In the AI-guided arm, lipid-lowering therapy use rose from 31% at baseline to 75% post-testing, compared with 32% to 47% in the usual care arm, with improved diagnostic certainty as the largest driver.
articles.result: Win ratio 2.00; lipid therapy use rose 31%→75% in AI arm

articles.title: DETECT-HF: Cordio Medical's Voice AI Predicts Heart Failure 24.6 Days Early in 563-Patient Pivotal Trial
articles.snippet: Cordio Medical's HearO smartphone system, using AI-driven voice signal processing, predicted more than 70% of heart failure events an average of 24.6 days before they occurred in a blinded, multicenter 563-patient study presented as late-breaking science at AHA 2026. Patient compliance was 85% for daily recordings, and no device-related adverse events were reported; the company now plans to file for FDA clearance ahead of a 2027 US commercial launch.
articles.result: >70% of HF events predicted avg. 24.6 days in advance

articles.title: AI ECHO INSIGHT Trial: AI Cuts Cardiologist Echocardiogram Review Time by 46% Across Kaiser Permanente Network
articles.snippet: A randomized study from 21 Kaiser Permanente Northern California medical centers found AI-drafted preliminary echocardiogram reports were noninferior to human drafts, with cardiologists unable to distinguish AI from sonographer reports in blinded review. Cardiologists spent an average of 4.6 minutes reviewing and finalizing AI-generated reports versus 8.5 minutes without AI — a 46% time reduction — with results presented as late-breaking science at AHA Scientific Sessions 2026.
articles.result: 46% reduction in cardiologist echo review time (8.5→4.6 min)

articles.title: Virtuoso Surgical Wins FDA De Novo Authorization for Robotic Endoscopy System for Bladder Tumor Resection
articles.snippet: The FDA granted de novo authorization on November 10, 2026 to Virtuoso Surgical's miniaturized robotic endoscopy platform — the first device in a new FDA classification for electromechanical endoluminal surgical systems. In the pivotal VIABLE study of 20 patients, the robot retrieved detrusor muscle in 94% of en bloc bladder lesion removals and evaluable margins in 93% of malignant lesions, surpassing the 60% performance goal and exceeding the ~70% median rate of conventional transurethral resections.
articles.result: 94% detrusor muscle retrieval vs ~70% historical benchmark

articles.title: Google AMIE Lancet Trial: Patient-Facing Diagnostic AI Completes 98 Real Primary Care Encounters With Zero Safety Stops
articles.snippet: Published in The Lancet on October 8, 2026, researchers at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center tested Google's AMIE conversational diagnostic AI with 114 enrolled patients (98 completing both AI interaction and primary care appointment) — marking the first prospective real-world study of patient-facing AI in primary care. Despite four predefined triggers allowing a supervising physician to halt any conversation, zero safety stops were triggered across all 98 encounters, and patients' attitudes toward AI improved after using the system.
articles.result: Zero safety stops across 98 real-world AI-patient encounters

articles.title: AEYE-DS Autonomous AI Boosts Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Adherence 69% at UMass Memorial in Four Months
articles.snippet: UMass Memorial Health's real-world EMR deployment of AEYE-DS — the FDA-cleared fully autonomous AI for diabetic retinopathy requiring just one image per eye — raised screening adherence from 29% to 49% within four months of go-live while cutting average exam time by 75% to under two minutes. The deployment was supported by CPT 92229 reimbursement with high claims approval rates and also improved HEDIS performance metrics.
articles.result: DR screening adherence rose 29%→49%; exam time cut 75%

articles.title: AEYE-DS Pivotal Trials Published: 99% Imageability and 100% Sensitivity for Severe DR Across 1,200+ Patients
articles.source: Frontiers in Digital Health / PR Newswire
articles.snippet: Three prospective controlled pivotal validation studies of AEYE-DS published in Frontiers in Digital Health demonstrated 92–93% sensitivity and 89–94% specificity for detecting more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy, with 99% imageability in non-mydriatic settings across both portable and tabletop cameras. Crucially, the system achieved 100% sensitivity for severe cases (ETDRS ≥43) across all three studies, and findings were formally recognized in the 2026 ADA Standards of Care.
articles.result: 99% imageability; 100% sensitivity for severe DR cases

articles.title: FDA Clears Bechtel Medical's Wound VOX — First 510(k)-Cleared Combined Negative Pressure and Topical Oxygen Wound System
articles.snippet: On November 10, 2026, the FDA issued 510(k) clearance to Bechtel Medical's Wound VOX, making it the first cleared device to integrate negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) and topical oxygen therapy (TOT) in a single platform. Bechtel Medical plans a limited commercial rollout in December 2026, targeting hard-to-heal wound patients who previously required two separate clinical systems.
articles.result: First FDA-cleared dual NPWT+oxygen system; rollout Dec 2026

articles.title: FDA Establishes New Class II Category for AI Software Predicting Cognitive Decline Progression to Alzheimer's
articles.snippet: Effective November 5, 2026, the FDA formally codified a new Class II device category for prognostic assessment software of mild cognitive impairment — prescription-only AI that combines multiple clinical data sources to estimate whether a diagnosed MCI patient will progress to Alzheimer's dementia within a specified period. The de novo classification order sets mandatory validation standards including independent test datasets, sensitivity, specificity, and PPV/NPV benchmarks, opening a regulated pathway for commercial deployment.
articles.result: New regulated Class II pathway opens for MCI-to-Alzheimer's AI

articles.title: FDA Classifies AI-Powered Digital Cervical Cytology Slide Imaging System as Class II Device
articles.source: FDA CDRH / Alston Health Care Week in Review
articles.snippet: On November 4, 2026, the FDA issued a final classification order establishing AI-assisted digital cervical cytology slide imaging as a Class II device, finding that classification provides reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness. The action creates a formal regulatory framework for autonomous or semi-autonomous AI tools applied to cervical cancer screening, enabling manufacturers to seek clearance via 510(k) with defined special controls.
articles.result: New Class II AI pathway created for cervical cancer screening

articles.title: Medidata State of AI in Clinical Trials 2026: Early Adopters Report 72.9% Trial Timeline Improvements
articles.snippet: Medidata's second annual State of AI in Clinical Trials report finds organizations with 18+ months of AI deployment experience report trial timeline improvements in 72.9% of cases and protocol deviation reduction in 67.5% of cases, far outpacing industry laggards. The report, covering responses from clinical operations leaders, also found that 86.5% of experienced adopters see measurable improvements in high-volume, rules-based workflows, and 92% of respondents across all experience levels are increasing AI investment.

articles.title: 2026 Meta-Analysis: AI Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Pathways Raise Referral Completion by 23.9% Globally
articles.snippet: A systematic review and meta-analysis published in npj Digital Medicine (Leigh et al., 2026) found that AI-assisted diabetic retinopathy screening pathways raised referral completion rates by 23.9% globally compared to standard of care, with AI screen-first models effectively tripling follow-up rates by isolating only the approximately 12% of patients who screen positive. The analysis reinforces real-world hospital deployment data showing AI can substantially reduce the gap between recommended and actual diabetic eye care.
articles.result: AI pathways raise DR referral completion 23.9%; ~3x follow-up
